page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the KVM hypervisor. The system is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.2 GHz. The memory configuration provides 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

Hardware accelerators and integrated storage are omitted in this instance profile. The ecs.c9i.4xlarge includes 0 GPUs and features no onboard local disk capacity, requiring workloads to rely exclusively on attached network block storage for operating system and data volumes. Networking performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The balanced compute-to-memory ratio delivers qualitative cost efficiency for scenarios where computational throughput is prioritized over massive memory capacities. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete dependency on remote storage networks and the absence of discrete GPU acceleration. The ecs.c9i.4xlarge is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as batch processing, application compilation pipelines, CI/CD runners, and distributed data transformation services.
